summary: Most placement failures occur when a boundary is cut before the clause's governing verb, subject, or hedging/reporting marker has arrived, forcing an isolated fragment to assert something the rest of the sentence overturns or a translator to invent missing subject/tone. Priority failures show up when a filler-adjacent or earliest-possible boundary is ranked top even though it leaves a large, unbalanced remainder, so tight budgets keep the riskier split; balanced mid-clause boundaries should rank higher. One case also violated format by leaking reasoning/text edits into the output.
